recommendations.name: West Route
recommendations.summary: Fold this row into the peak's Northeast Face route and keep only its long southern hike-in from Salmon La Sac as a second way to reach that route; no separate west-side climb exists.
recommendations.detail: No source documents a west ridge or west face route on Little Big Chief. The only published accounts that use this row's Waptus River / Chief Creek approach go on to the Dutch Miller Gap area and climb the Northeast Face, which is the peak's easiest line and its 1939 first-ascent route (class 3-4, with an exposed notch on the north/northeast ridge). The row's own beta and pitch table already describe that Northeast Face line, from a Williams Lake camp, and its 'Northwest Face' face/NW aspect were copied from the separate Falcon Route row. Merge it into wa_little_big_chief_mountain_northeast_face. What is worth carrying over is the Salmon La Sac / Waptus River Trail approach (approach_variants[0], the trailhead-to-Chief-Creek waypoints, road, the Cle Elum district access/permit/emergency details and the Waptus ford hazard), added as a second approach to the Northeast Face. Drop the invented 'west ridge/west face' climbing_route, descent_text and the 'west gully' itinerary day.

recommendations.name: South Ridge
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the usual route: the long way in over Buck Creek Pass and the High Pass high route to a camp in Louis Creek Basin, then up the south and southwest side. Rewrite the parts that describe the shorter King Lake route instead.
recommendations.detail: Both lines are real, but published sources call the west-side approach the 'normal route'. You reach the south and southwest slopes either on the high route south from Buck Creek Pass (camp in Louis Creek Basin) or over Little Giant Pass. The club lists this line as its 'Southwest Route' scramble, and a detailed trip report climbs it from a Louis Creek Basin camp. The King Lake line, up to the east-ridge notch and the southeast slopes, is a rarely used shortcut through the Buck Creek burn and is better known as the start of the harder northeast face. The row's approach, approach_variants, descent_text and climbing_route already describe the Buck Creek Pass line. The beta, the pitch table, all three itinerary days and the timing notes describe King Lake and need rewriting. Two waypoint pins (the 'basin' and the 'snowfield', both east of the summit near Trinity) match neither line and need moving to Louis Creek Basin and the upper south slopes. The owner may also want to rename the row 'Southwest Route' to match the common name. The King Lake line could be kept as a short mention in approach_variants.

recommendations.name: Standard Scramble (Esmeralda Basin)
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the standard De Roux Creek scramble, where you leave the trail at a house-sized boulder and climb about 1,100 ft of scree. Rewrite every part that sends climbers over Fortune Creek Pass from Esmeralda Basin, and drop 'Esmeralda Basin' from the name.
recommendations.detail: Every source found (the peak's route page, the hiking-association page and a detailed trip report) gives one standard route. It starts at the De Roux trailhead (~3,800 ft) and follows the Boulder-De Roux trail west between Esmeralda and Koppen. You leave the trail at the house-sized boulder at the last switchback (~5,600 ft), then climb about 1,100 ft of Class 2 scree to the west summit: roughly 7 mi and 3,100 ft round trip. No source describes a scramble up from Fortune Creek Pass, which is about 1.8 km north of the summit. The row's beta, pitch_detail, face and approach_variants already describe De Roux. The overview's last sentence, approach, descent, descent_text, climbing_route, bail, pro_tips, the itinerary and timing, and the Esmeralda Basin waypoints all describe the Fortune Creek Pass line and need rewriting. The trailhead waypoint should become the De Roux trailhead, and gain and distance should follow the De Roux figures (~3,100 ft, ~7 mi). A fitting name is 'Southwest Slope via De Roux Creek'.

recommendations.name: Southeast Slopes
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the standard summer scramble from Denny Creek over Hemlock Pass, which comes up the southwest side and not the southeast. Rewrite the parts that describe the Alpental and Source Lake gully, a steeper line mostly climbed in winter.
recommendations.detail: The club's published scramble for Bryant starts at the Denny Creek trailhead (2,300 ft) and goes to Hemlock Pass. From there it follows the ridge on a 33 degree bearing to a meadow below the talus and finishes on loose rock around the summit block. That is 9.5 mi and 3,900 ft for Bryant plus Hemlock Peak (about 9 mi / 3,600 ft for Bryant alone), and trip logs and a mapped trail agree. The row's beta, itinerary, timing, bail and trailhead-waypoint note already describe this line. The Alpental / Source Lake / Great Scott Basin approach to the steep Bryant-Chair gully is real, but it appears mainly as a winter scramble and is an avalanche path. It can stay as a secondary approach variant. It should not be the main approach, the climbing route or the descent. The face and aspect should be southwest. The approach, climbing_route, descent_text, hazards, overview last sentence, approach_logistics and waypoints 0-6 need rewriting to the Denny Creek line. Waypoint 0 should be the Denny Creek trailhead at 2,300 ft. gain_ft/distance should use the Bryant-only figure if one is confirmed, or the paired-peak figure labelled as such.

recommendations.name: South Route
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the documented climb from the West Fork Foss lakes: up past Chetwoot and Iron Cap lakes to the west and north ridges. Rewrite the parts that describe a long Middle Fork Snoqualmie / Williams Lake approach, and rename it, since there is no south route.
recommendations.detail: Every trip report found reaches Iron Cap from the West Fork Foss River trail off US 2, going past Trout, Copper and Big Heart lakes (~7.3 mi, ~3,300 ft to Big Heart) to Chetwoot / Iron Cap Lake. From there parties climb talus to the west ridge or around the north ridge, with a short class 3 notch and a ramp to the north ridge. One more report follows a high route in from Big Snow by the same lakes. No source describes climbing Iron Cap from Dutch Miller Gap, Williams Lake or La Bohn Gap; the one report that touches Williams Lake only walks out that way after the summit. The row's beta, bail, rope_note, climbing_route, approach_variants and trailhead-waypoint note already describe the Chetwoot line. The approach, the itinerary (three days), timing, waypoints 0-6 (Middle Fork footbridge through the Williams Lake saddle, and the Dingford Creek trailhead), approach_logistics, overview and descent_text describe the Middle Fork corridor and need rewriting to the West Fork Foss trailhead. gain_ft and dist_km need recomputing from that trailhead. The name and aspect should become something like 'West Ridge / North Ridge via Chetwoot Lake', aspect W/N. One note: a current report says FR 6835 to the West Fork Foss trailhead is damaged and needs a ~2.4 mi road walk, which should be confirmed before it is written into the road field.
